title: potaterrr — automation field notes
description: What broke while building AI voice receptionists, invoice agents, lead retrieval pipelines and scrapers.

items.title: How an AI receptionist answers a clinic's missed call
items.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of what happens when a clinic misses a call: the voice agent picks up, captures intake, checks the calendar, books the slot, logs the call and alerts the front desk, with the human checkpoints left in.

items.title: What an AI receptionist actually costs a small clinic
items.summary: Where the money goes when a clinic adds an AI receptionist: voice minutes, the automation layer, the one-time build, what moves each line, and how to compare quotes without getting anchored on a fake number.

items.title: AI receptionist for a small clinic: what it can and can't do
items.summary: A practical breakdown for clinic owners: the calls an AI receptionist should handle, the ones it must hand to a human, the decisions to make before launch, and how to test it on scripted calls before a real patient hears it.

items.title: HIPAA-compliant AI receptionist: what healthcare actually needs
items.summary: A practical checklist for clinics weighing voice AI: what counts as PHI in a phone call, the five controls that actually matter, the questions to ask any vendor, and the red flags that mean walk away.

items.title: The call is the evidence: building Sales Call QA
items.summary: Building an n8n sales-call QA pipeline: a five-part rubric, quote verification that actually matches the transcript, a no-objection rule, a Gemini token budget bug, and a review gate that only wakes a manager when the call is risky.

items.title: job-scrapper now posts to Discord with Gemini summaries
items.summary: How job-scrapper moved from Make.com to a self-contained GitHub Actions pipeline: Gemini summaries, Discord embeds, dedupe, and a 4-hour cadence.

items.title: The invoice chaser: three bugs, one rule
items.summary: Building an n8n accounts-receivable agent that drafts overdue invoice reminders: Gemini returning an empty response to a structured parser, a signature the model kept rewriting, a cooldown that had to exist, and the one rule that shaped all of it.

items.title: My dotfiles, one line
items.summary: How a single curl | sh installs Bash, Neovim, Starship, Fastfetch, Hyprland, Waybar, Wofi and GTK on six distro families — a bootstrap script plus GNU Stow.

items.title: When "free tier" means zero: folklore video and the Gemini quota wall
items.summary: The folklore topic queue works and the scripts draft themselves, then video generation hits a hard 429. Building a free AI folklore-video pipeline on Make.com.

items.title: Feeding Make.com from Python
items.summary: How job-scrapper turns OnlineJobs.ph listings into clean webhook payloads for Make.com: flat JSON design, polite scraping, retries, and queue discipline.

items.title: The free-plan ops math
items.summary: Make.com's free plan gives you 1,000 operations a month. Here's the arithmetic that decides whether your polling interval is an automation or an ops bonfire.

items.title: One receptionist, three engines
items.summary: I built the same AI clinic receptionist on Make, n8n and Zapier. Here's what broke, what shone, and which automation engine to pick for whom. A HIPAA-compliant build is available.

items.title: Why my AI never sends emails
items.summary: The human-in-the-loop pattern behind Dead Lead Retrieval: LLM drafts, Gmail holds, human approves. Guardrails, war stories and the case for keeping judgment out of the loop's hands.
